liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Unbroken Chain** (4 reviews): First take breaks down after a Keith mistake; Jerry jokingly sentences him to laps, then a full vocal run-through follows; Another version is Phil alone on acoustic guitar, singing and calling out chord changes [3][4][12][13]
- **Crazy Fingers** (2 reviews): Named among the highlights of the tape; Reviewer finds a great version of it on this tape [6][10]
- **Pride of Cucamonga** (2 reviews): Reviewer's favorite Mars Hotel song; since the band never played it live, hearing it here matters; Reviewer says Phil performed it live the previous summer, possibly at Hartford [8][9]
- **Ship of Fools** (1 review): Described as mixing acoustic and electric instruments; counted as a highlight [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **Pride of Cucamonga**: rare: 4 archived performances [14]
- **Money Money**: rare: 7 archived performances [14]
- **Pride of Cucamonga**: rare: 4 archived performances [14]
- **Money Money**: rare: 7 archived performances [14]
- **Pride of Cucamonga**: rare: 4 archived performances [14]
- **Money Money**: rare: 7 archived performances [14]

## The recordings

- **gd74-12-xx.mars-hotel.12468.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 99 min; rated 4.23/5 by 22 [1]. Said about its sound: This copy has more reverb than the box set version, suggesting someone remixed it; Sound quality is mediocre; Reviewer once had a tape of this material with much better quality than this copy [4][6][7][10][13]

## Around the show

- These are rehearsal recordings, never intended for public listening [8]
- Recordings capture the band's creative process at Front Street, like being a fly on the wall [12]
- The shn file was linked to the wrong gig entry and needed correcting [1]
- Some versions here are judged better than those on the released Mars Hotel album, which is considered overproduced [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd74-12-xx.mars-hotel.12468.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard source transferred through an unknown generation to CDR, labeled Mars Hotel Outtakes [1]
